summary: Adversarially verify the 15 shared-infra perf/stability/a11y fixes for regressions before commit

all.change: apps/shared/react/hooks/useStateBindings.ts — getSnapshot changed from a loop calling .get() on every state observable (discarding results, returning revisionRef.current) to () => revisionRef.current; [state] dep dropped from its useCallback.
all.reasoning: The removed loop never affected change detection: the old getSnapshot ALWAYS returned revisionRef.current regardless of the .get() calls (their results were discarded), so React's Object.is comparison only ever saw a new snapshot when revisionRef.current was incremented. That increment happens exclusively in subscribeCombined's wrappedOnChange (revisionRef.current++ then onStoreChange — lines 71-80), which is fully intact and independent of the removed loop. So re-renders still fire on every observable change, and MiniAppRoot adds a second redundant trigger via its stateVersion subscription on every state observable (MiniAppRoot.tsx:355-362). The accessors str/num/bool/val call state[key]?.get() live during render (lines 87-100), and createDerived.get IS compute (context.ts:62), so every derived recomputes on demand each render — the loop's only effect (recompute-and-discard) was pure waste. I verified all sampled createDerived compute bodies (last-survivor, wallet-health, gas-sponsor, self-loan) are pure (formatting/arithmetic/comparison); .set() calls live only in async actions, never in derived compute, so no eager-evaluation side effect was lost. The hardest case — last-survivor's per-second clock — confirms safety: only the derived `countdown` is in the state record (not `now`/`timeRemainingSeconds`); createDerived.subscribe chains listeners through deps so now.set(Date.now()) propagates to the state-record observable's subscribers and drives re-render independent of getSnapshot, with str(\"countdown\") reading live on render. Across consumers, accessors are called at render top and effects consume captured values (idiomatic React), so no PlayArea reads a derived only in a non-render path that depended on the loop. getServerSnapshot is the same ref-returning fn (SSR-safe); dropping [state] cannot stale a function that only returns a useRef. react-context.test.ts + last-survivor/wallet-health/gas-sponsor playarea tests (15 tests, incl. reactive re-render + clock) pass.

all.change: MiniAppRoot.tsx wraps the shared `playArea` element in <ErrorBoundary t fallback onError onRetry> (apps/shared/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx), covering both the standalone (StandaloneDappSurface) and shell (MiniAppPage) render paths.
all.reasoning: Verified all 6 points against actual code. (1) Props: the diff is a pure re-indent — all 10 PlayArea props (t, state, dispatch, services, status, setStatus, clearStatus, loadError, retryLoad, launchContext) are byte-identical; none dropped. (2) Success path: ErrorBoundary.render() (line 95) returns `children` directly with NO DOM wrapper — a class component returning a single element is DOM-transparent, so `.section-hero > *` / `.standalone-dapp-root .play-area` selectors still resolve to PlayArea's own root. Grep found ZERO apps using direct-child combinators on section-hero/content-main/play-area, and the standalone reset stylesheet uses descendant (not child) selectors, so even those are unaffected. (3) No double-fallback: MiniAppPage's renderContent() try/catch around `return children` is dead for render errors (React render throws propagate through the fiber tree, not as a sync exception in that try block); the inner real ErrorBoundary catches first and renders in place — no conflict. (4) onRetry=reloadData (line 290) and onError=handleBoundaryError (line 467) are both useCallback-wrapped → stable references, so the ErrorBoundary instance is reused and preserves hasError across benign parent re-renders. (5) StrictMode/remount: handleRetry resets {hasError:false}; a genuine remount re-runs the constructor with hasError:false — standard ErrorBoundary semantics, not stuck. (6) No circular import: NeoButton imports only react + its own SCSS; components-react/index.ts does not import MiniAppRoot or ErrorBoundary. Extra: all fallback i18n keys (errorFallback, errorTitle, retry, reset, unexpectedError) exist in base-messages.ts and are auto-merged into every app, so the fallback never shows raw keys. The two apps that `throw new Error` (private-transfer, wallet-health) do so inside async handlers wrapped in try/catch — not render-phase — so the new render boundary cannot alter their behavior. tsc on apps/shared/tsconfig.json shows no errors in MiniAppRoot.tsx, ErrorBoundary.tsx, or MiniAppPage.tsx (the surfaced tsc errors are pre-existing, in unrelated gas-lucky-pool/last-survivor Vue composables).

all.change: apps/shared/services/BalanceService.ts — useBalance().refresh() now invalidates the per-asset balance cache key before calling getBalance(), so event-driven refreshes always read fresh from chain instead of being masked by the 15s TTL cache.
all.reasoning: Read the diff, full BalanceService.ts, CacheService.ts, EventBus.ts, ChainService.address, and context.ts createObservable. (1) No infinite loop: the only triggers of refresh() are the EventBus subscriptions to BALANCE_CHANGED and TRANSACTION_CONFIRMED. The terminal step balance.set() is a plain createObservable setter (context.ts:37-41) that only notifies local re-render listeners — it never emits any EventBus event. Chain: event→refresh→invalidate→getBalance(readBalance + cache.set)→balance.set→React re-render. Terminates. (2) Key derivation matches exactly: refresh computes owner = this.chain.address.get() ?? undefined (line 128); getBalance with no address arg computes owner = address ?? this.chain.address.get() ?? undefined where address is undefined, reducing to the identical expression off the same addressObservable. Line 130 calls getBalance synchronously immediately after the invalidate on line 129 (no await between), so the address cannot change in between, and balanceCacheKey(asset, owner) is identical for invalidate and the subsequent get/set. CacheService applies its neo:appId: prefix consistently in invalidate/get/set, so prefixing doesn't desync. (3) Initial refresh() invalidating an empty cache is harmless: memory.delete on a missing key is a no-op and localStorage.removeItem on an absent key is harmless. (4) Concurrent useBalance instances for the same asset: each invalidate+cache-check runs synchronously before yielding at the readBalance await, so multiple instances may each read chain on the same event — but that is the intended correctness fix (avoid serving the stale cached value), not a regression; pre-change behavior would have wrongly served the stale value. (5) One-shot getBalance callers are unchanged and still benefit from the cache. Build 60/60 and 889 vitest already pass; no test asserts the old stale-cache-on-refresh behavior.

all.change: EdgeClient.ts: (a) fetch now passes signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30000); (b) success-path res.json() now has .catch(() => ({})).
all.reasoning: Verified all four concerns against actual code + callers + a live probe in the jsdom test env. (1) AbortSignal.timeout exists in Node v24.4.1 and jsdom (probe confirmed typeof === "function" and abort yields TimeoutError); pattern already used identically in apps/shared/composables/useMorpheusDataFeed.ts:75; Baseline-available in all modern browsers since 2022. No ReferenceError. (2) A timeout abort rejects fetch; no caller switches on error.name (no isOsBoundaryError helper exists in repo — it was speculative in the prompt). Every consumer wraps proxy calls in generic try/catch (verified useCheckin.ts:330 recordFailure/console.warn, useRedEnvelope.ts, etc.). A timeout rejection is handled identically to the pre-existing network/DNS-failure rejections from the same await this.call(...) path — no new crash surface. (3) res.json().catch(()=>({}) ) yields {}: resolveInvocationIntent({}) returns null (empty scriptHash/operation) so submitWalletIntentIfPresent returns {} as-is with no spurious wallet sign and no throw; envelope check ("ok" in {}) is false so {} returns as T. Mirrors the existing error-path .catch. The existing coverage test passes json:()=>Promise.resolve(undefined) which resolves (not rejects) so .catch never fires — behavior unchanged there. (4) 30s is generous vs the 10s used for the comparable Neo RPC in useMorpheusDataFeed; edge endpoints (auth, balance, RPC reads, intent construction) are interactive request/response, not long-poll/SSE/batch — none legitimately exceed 30s. Ran both os-proxies test files: 67/67 pass. Tests mock fetch and ignore the signal, so the timeout path itself is untested, but its construction is exercised and the rejection semantics are well-established and consumer-handled.

all.change: ClipboardService now emits notifications on NOTIFICATION_EVENT ("platform:notification") imported from NotificationService, instead of the bare "notification" string; its test was updated to subscribe on the same constant.
all.reasoning: Verified all five sub-questions against the actual code. (1) MiniAppRoot.tsx:305-312 subscribes on NOTIFICATION_EVENT and reads notification.message + notification.type; clipboard emits {message, type:"success"|"error"} which fully satisfies the Notification interface (duration is optional and unused). NotificationType ("success"|"error"|...) is a subset of StatusType ("success"|"error"|"warning"|"info"|"danger"|"loading") that setStatus accepts, so no type mismatch. (2) Grep across apps/ for "notification"/'notification' found ZERO remaining listeners — the only hit is the new explanatory comment, so nothing goes silent. (3) No duplicate toast: ConsoleToolPanel.copyPayload only delegates to services.clipboard.copy() with no own emit; FactoryPlayArea uses an independent navigator.clipboard.writeText + local-state path that never touches the bus. Only two emitters of NOTIFICATION_EVENT exist (NotificationService, ClipboardService). (4) No circular import: ClipboardService -> NotificationService -> (type-only) EventBus -> nothing; the EventBus import in NotificationService is `import type` (erased at runtime), and there is no path back to ClipboardService. (5) Test is not a tautology: it imports the same NOTIFICATION_EVENT constant, asserts exactly one emission with the precise {message,type} payload; if the channel were wrong the array would be empty and the test would fail. The new test now matches the channel MiniAppRoot actually listens on, whereas the old test (on "notification") passed while masking the production bug. EventBus.emit is synchronous with per-handler try/catch isolation, so no ordering/reentrancy concern. This is a genuine bug fix (copy toasts were silently dropped before because the listener was already on NOTIFICATION_EVENT); the only behavioral change is that copy success/failure toasts now correctly appear — intended, not a regression.

all.change: transfer-payment-guards: (a) TransferService.scaleAmount now does Number(amount), rejecting !isFinite||<0 for ALL assets (NEO+GAS) before scaling; (b) wallet-sdk-composables payGAS now rejects !isFinite||<=0 (was !isFinite only).
all.reasoning: Traced every consumer of both changed functions. (1) CALLERS: TransferService's public API (transferGas/transferNeo/transferToken) has ZERO app callers across all 60 apps — only its own internal methods and one toBeDefined() assertion in PlatformServices.test.ts; so scaleAmount's stricter guard is dead-path hardening with no live consumer. payGAS's only real consumer is useContractInteraction.invoke (line 152); but that `invoke` method itself has ZERO consumers (apps use invokeWithDirectPrepaidGas/invokeDirectly, and the only reference to `invoke` outside its definition is a JSDoc comment). invokeWithDirectPrepaidGas does NOT route through payGAS — it builds the transfer args directly with base units — so the payment-sent test passing "100000000" is unaffected (confirmed by reading lines 248-284). No app/test passes "0"/""/negative to payGAS, transferGas, transferNeo, transferToken, or processPayment (grep returned nothing). (2) Number() vs parseFloat(): the only behavioral difference (trailing-garbage like "1.5abc" → NaN throw instead of 1.5) applies to the GAS branch of scaleAmount, which has no app callers; no test relies on trailing-garbage tolerance and no test asserts the changed message strings ("Invalid transfer amount"/"Invalid amount"/PAYMENT_INVALID_AMOUNT — grep found none). (3) NEO indivisible path: valid integers truncate identically (Number("5")=5 → Math.trunc → "5"); "0" still passes since the guard is <0 not <=0, matching prior unguarded behavior. Pre-change, a malformed NEO amount produced String(Math.trunc(NaN))="NaN" (a corrupt Integer arg); now it throws early — strictly an improvement. (4) GAS_MULTIPLIER unchanged at 100000000 and the ×1e8 scaling expression (Math.round(parsed*GAS_MULTIPLIER)) is byte-identical to before; constants file unmodified. (5) payGAS <=0 boundary: pre-change accepted 0 (would broadcast a 0-value GAS transfer) and negatives (would be rejected by the wallet anyway); new guard blocks both at the source — intended hardening, no caller relied on submitting zero/negative payments. Ran the three most relevant test files (wallet-sdk-nep21, contract-interaction.payment-sent, PlatformServices) from apps/shared with the correct vitest config: 28/28 pass. (An isolated run from the repo root showed window-undefined errors — that is a jsdom-environment config artifact of running outside apps/shared, not related to the change.)

all.change: app-local-guards: (a) neo-treasury treasury.ts Number()+isFinite guard, (b) red-envelope mapStoredEnvelope toFinite coercion, (c) neo-convert useNeoConvert.ts eventBus.on(EventBus.BALANCE_CHANGED) + value import of EventBus
all.reasoning:
(a) neo-treasury: b.amount is typed string and getnep17balances returns integer base-unit strings (no decimal point). For such strings Number(s) === parseInt(s), so NEO=amount (old parseInt/1 was a no-op /1, equivalent) and GAS=amount/1e8 are identical for all valid inputs. The only behavior change is for malformed amounts: old parseInt('' | null | 'abc') => NaN poisoned the totals; new path coerces ''/null to 0 (Number('' ?? 0)=0, finite) or skips truly non-numeric via continue. Strict improvement. No treasury tests reference this code.

(b) red-envelope: StoredEnvelope numeric fields are typed number and come from normalized StorageProxy JSON, so toFinite is a pure pass-through for every valid value (Number.isFinite true => returns n unchanged) — identical to the old Number(...??0). It only diverges for corrupted non-finite values, mapping NaN=>0 instead of leaving NaN. remainingPackets = Math.max(0, packetCount-openedCount) can no longer render 'NaN'. The envelope is still returned (not dropped). Note: a corrupted-packetCount record now computes depleted=true (0>=0) hence active/canOpen=false, vs the old NaN comparisons yielding depleted=false — but that path only triggers on corrupt data and presenting an uninterpretable envelope as openable was itself buggy; valid envelopes are bit-identical. No red-envelope tests reference these symbols.

(c) neo-convert: Verified EventBus.BALANCE_CHANGED = 'platform:balance:changed' (EventBus.ts:37), which is exactly what TransferService emits (TransferService.ts:75,114) and what BalanceService.useBalance subscribes to. The old bare 'BALANCE_CHANGED' literal never matched, so syncNeo/syncGas only ran once at setup and never on subsequent balance changes — the fix makes them fire. EventBus is exported as a value (export class EventBus; re-exported in services/index.ts:31), so the value import compiles and satisfies both the value usage (EventBus.BALANCE_CHANGED) and the type usage (eventBus: EventBus); build 60/60 confirms. Grep across apps/ (excluding node_modules/dist) shows no remaining bare 'BALANCE_CHANGED'/'platform:balance:changed' subscription — the only match is inside the new explanatory comment. neo-convert has no test files, so nothing depended on the old broken behavior. A minor timing subtlety (syncNeo fires synchronously and may read a one-event-stale watcher value because useBalance.refresh is async) is not a regression: it strictly improves on the prior never-updating behavior and the watcher's async refresh converges.

all.change: scss-a11y: ConsoleToolPanel.scss select :focus→:focus-visible (line 311) + new summary:focus-visible focus ring (lines 440-444); _playarea-base.scss badge--warning color #b9791a→var(--ns-warning-strong,#b9791a); --ns-warning-strong:#b9791a added once to theme-base.scss :root.
all.reasoning: Read all three diffs, the surrounding SCSS, callers, and the built CSS. (1) :focus-visible is widely supported (all evergreen browsers); the select still gets a ring on keyboard nav (superset of :focus matches keyboard focus) and intentionally not on mouse click — confirmed in dist CSS. The summary is a native <details>/<summary> pair (ConsoleToolPanel.tsx:252-253), natively focusable, so the new focus ring works without tabindex. (2) The new .console-tool__payload-card > summary:focus-visible rule is placed before the ::after rule and only sets outline/border-radius/box-shadow on a :focus-visible state — it cannot override the existing base summary styles (different pseudo-state, and it touches only properties the base rule doesn't set). (3) --ns-warning-strong:#b9791a is defined exactly once in theme-base.scss :root (verified via grep across all of apps/ minus node_modules/dist), is NOT redefined in [data-theme=dark] or any prefers-color-scheme block, and the var() fallback is also #b9791a — so the badge--warning color resolves to #b9791a identically before and after = zero visual change across all 60 apps. Brand green #16c784 untouched (--ns-brand, focus-ring rgba(22,199,132) unchanged). Build compiled cleanly: dist CSS for oracle-vrf-console and oracle-seal-console contains select:focus-visible, summary:focus-visible, and warning-strong. One non-blocking nuance (see failingScenario): two apps (oracle-vrf-console, oracle-http-console) have their own per-app .console-tool__field select:focus rule that loads AFTER the shared rule with equal specificity, so in those two apps the ring still shows on mouse click — but that is pre-existing behavior, not a regression, and keyboard accessibility is preserved (ring still shows on keyboard). The minor radius-sm fallback mismatch (rule says 8px, token is 12px) only affects the summary focus-ring corner radius with no prior baseline, so it cannot regress anything.
all.failingScenario: none (non-regression note: oracle-vrf-console/PlayArea.scss:107 and oracle-http-console/PlayArea.scss:118 still define .console-tool__field select:focus, which loads after the shared :focus-visible at equal specificity, so the select focus ring still appears on mouse click in those 2 apps — the keyboard-only intent is unrealized there, but this is unchanged prior behavior and no a11y is lost; the other console apps get the intended keyboard-only ring.)
